intro.sudokuCaption: An illustration of the idea behind SHREK-HRM: a model that fills in the grid, spots its own mistakes and corrects them. Research project with two fellow students.

project1.title: The SUPER Assessor
project1.summary: Developed as a part of the full-stack web development course in 2024, the project was developed with 2 students from my class. The application helps teachers create and evaluate assessment forms using a card-based game. Application is built using the MERN stack.
project1.short: A card-based tool where teachers create and evaluate assessment schemes. Full-stack app built in a group of three.
project1.imageAlt: SUPER Assessor shown on a laptop and a tablet

project2.title: Travel Website with a Focus on Accessibility
project2.summary: For the course accessibility, usability, and ethics course, I built a travel-themed website that focuses on accessible and inclusive design. The goal was to build a website that users with various disabilities could navigate and interact with easily, following the WCAG guidelines (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines).
project2.short: A travel website built to WCAG and tested with screen readers and keyboard navigation.
project2.imageAlt: The travel website shown on a laptop

project3.title: E-Learning Platform for the Shared Model
project3.summary: For the bachelor's project we developed an e-learning platform for the Shared Model. Me and 2 other students worked in collaboration with Helseinn and Helsefelleskapet Innlandet and the goal was to make training in the shared model in the healthcare and municipal sector in Innlandet more accessible and effective through user-friendly design, interactive modules, and research-based content.
project3.short: An e-learning platform that makes training in the Shared Model easier for the health and municipal sector in Innlandet. We interviewed the target group, tested three different prototypes with them and built the platform around what users preferred. Instead of ready-made tools like H5P, we built our own course builder, giving us full control over design and content. Bachelor's project with Helseinn, built in a group of three.
project3.imageAlt: Illustration of the Shared Model from HelseInn

project4.title: SHREK-HRM: Self-Correcting Hierarchical Reasoning Models
project4.summary: A research project at OsloMet together with two fellow students. We extended Hierarchical Reasoning Models with self-correction mechanisms, such as error injection and stagnation-aware halting, and evaluated them on the Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Hard benchmarks. The models were trained on an NVIDIA GH200 GPU on the Simula Research Laboratory cluster. I wrote most of the paper and worked on the code through pair programming.
project4.imageAlt: A maze with the solution path highlighted in cyan
project4.short: Reasoning models that detect and correct their own mistakes, tested on Sudoku and mazes. Research project at OsloMet, trained on Simula's GPU cluster.

project5.title: 3D Shape Classification
project5.summary: For the course 3D Computer Vision, I built and compared three classifiers on a subset of ShapeNetCore: a 3D CNN on voxels, a graph neural network on meshes with PyTorch3D, and PointNet on point clouds. The project compares how the different 3D representations affect accuracy and training cost.
project5.imageAlt: A chair represented as a 3D point cloud
project5.short: Three models that recognise 3D objects from voxels, meshes and point clouds, compared on ShapeNetCore.

about.description1: I have a bachelor's degree in web development from NTNU Gjøvik, and I'm now taking a master's in Applied AI at OsloMet, graduating in June 2027.
about.description2: I come from Bødalen, a town outside Asker. Technology has been an interest of mine since I was young, and I started studying web development in 2022. During the bachelor's I found that I enjoyed backend work the most, especially APIs and databases, and that curiosity about what happens behind the interface led me to AI. In the master's I have worked with deep learning, 3D computer vision and reinforcement learning, which is the area I find most exciting right now. I like solving challenges and building solutions that actually make a difference, and I enjoy the combination of understanding the models and building something useful around them.
about.description3: In my free time I enjoy working out and being social. I enjoy traveling and experiencing new cultures and i'm always looking for opportunities to develop myself.
